title: FHE-CGRA: Enable Efficient Acceleration of Fully Homomorphic Encryption on CGRAs
problem: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) incurs significant performance and memory costs due to intensive computations. FHE-ML applications require different encryption variants across stages with varying optimal hardware execution unit designs, making fixed-architecture accelerators inefficient.
motivation: FHE enables privacy-preserving computation on encrypted data but remains impractical for ML applications due to prohibitive performance overhead, necessitating efficient adaptive hardware acceleration.
method: FHE-CGRA uses a coarse-grained reconfigurable architecture (CGRA) — hardware whose processing units can be rewired to perform different computational tasks — that changes its configuration while running. Since each stage of ML inference uses different encryption methods with different optimization requirements, the hardware execution units reconfigure themselves to match each stage's specific operations. An MLIR compiler toolchain (software that converts ML code into hardware-level instructions) automatically coordinates this reconfiguration and optimizes resource use across all stages.
key_novelty: The core idea is using a CGRA whose execution units reconfigure themselves during operation to match whatever FHE encryption method and operation each stage of ML inference requires.
contributions: FHE-CGRA framework combining CGRA architecture with FHE-optimized execution units for homomorphic ML acceleration
MLIR-based compiler toolchain for end-to-end compilation and optimization of homomorphic ML applications
Achieves 8.15x speedup over conventional CGRA baseline for FHE-CNN inference
Delivers 16.48x power efficiency improvement versus state-of-the-art FPGA-based FHE accelerators

metrics.speedup: 8.15x vs conventional CGRA; 16.48x power efficiency vs FPGA-based FHE-CNN accelerator

limitations: Scalability to larger models, datasets, and FHE parameter choices not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: reconfigurable hardware acceleration for encrypted machine learning
